questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. **

P- Epistemological idealists (such as Kant) might insist that the only things which can be directly known for certain are ideas. 

Q- The approach to idealism by Western philosophers has been different to that of Eastern thinkers. 

R- In much of Western thought (though not in such major Western thinkers as Plato and Hegel) the ideal relates to direct knowledge of subjective mental ideas, or images. 

S- It is then usually juxtaposed with realism in which the real is said to have an absolute existence prior to and independent of our knowledge.
questions.solution: The given para-jumbled sentence is based on the topic of idealism by western philosophers. Therefore, the first statement should be Q which introduces the topic. The second statement R, it has continued to what the first statement has said. The third statement is developing the topic even more by elaborating what the topic is conveying.The last statement culminates the topic by giving a valid example.The correct option is option 4.

questions.question:
** In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. **

Karnataka grows coffee

options.text: Coffee is being grown in Karnataka.
Let the coffee be grown in Karnataka.

questions.solution: The sentence is in simple present tense. The rule to convert it in passive voice is Object(coffee) + is/are/am +V3 (grown) +preposition(in) + subject(Karnataka).From this rule, the correct transformation should be Coffee is grown in Karnataka.the correct option is option 3.

questions.question:
** In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. **

Gopal's mother reminded him to take his wallet.

options.text: “Are you going to take your wallet or not?” said Gopal to his mother.
“Don't forget to take your wallet, Gopal” said his mother.
Gopal's mother said, “Remember your wallet, Gopal?
“Here is your wallet Gopal” said his mother.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**“Don't forget to take your wallet, Gopal” said his mother.' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** 

__
 
• The direct speech equivalent of "Gopal's mother reminded him to take his wallet" involves a form of address where the mother is directly speaking to Gopal about not forgetting his wallet.
 
• The option uses an imperative sentence, ("Don't forget"), which is fitting for a reminder.
 
• The direct address, "Gopal," correctly places this as a communication between Gopal and his mother, aligning with the original sentence structure.
 
• This choice naturally translates the indirect reminder into direct speech without altering the original message or tone.
 
• The inclusion of "said his mother" after the quote maintains the attribution to Gopal's mother, preserving the context.
 
• It directly captures the essence of a reminder through the use of an imperative form, which is often used in direct speech for such purposes.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Option 1 misrepresents the nature of the reminder as a question about intention, rather than a reminder.
 
• Option 3 incorrectly formats the direct speech as a question, altering the intended reminder nature of the sentence.
 
• Option 4 suggests the mother is handing the wallet to Gopal, rather than reminding him, which changes the original meaning.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence. **

If (you will approach) her sincerely, she will listen to your problem definitely.
questions.solution:
This is a conditional sentence with a possible condition and its probable result. These sentences are based on facts and are used to make statements about the real world. The zero conditional uses **if **or **when** and must be followed by the simple present or imperative.

The correct option is option 1.

**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence. **

The mobile phones have made digital cameras a little (superfluous) in today's world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Obsolete". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **“Superfluous” **means unnecessary or extra. It does not fit in the context of the sentence.
 
• **“Extinct” **means no longer in existence. It does not fit in the context of the sentence.
 
• **“Redundant” **means unnecessary or superfluous. It is a synonym of “obsolete”.
 
• **“Obsolete” **means no longer in use or out of date. It fits in the context of the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1) “extinct”: “Extinct” means no longer in existence.
 
 
• It does not fit in the context of the sentence because digital cameras are still in existence.
 
 
 
• Option 3) “redundancy”: “Redundancy” means unnecessary or superfluous.
 
 
• It is a synonym of “obsolete”. However, “obsolete” is a more common and appropriate word to use in this context.
 
 
 
• Option 4) “No improvement”: The sentence is incorrect. It should be “The mobile phones have made digital cameras obsolete in today's world”.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. **

Ankita is disgusted _____ the habit of her brother.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**with**__**.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Disgust__: feeling or expressing revulsion or strong disapproval.

 __
 
• Example__: *She was disgusted with the decision.*
 
 

__
 
• **Let's see the usage of different prepositions with disgust**

 
 
• disgusted (at/by somebody/something). Example: *I was disgusted at/by the sight.*
 
• disgusted (with somebody/something/yourself) Example: *I was disgusted with myself for eating so much.*
 
• disgusted (to see, hear, etc…) Example: *He was disgusted to see such awful living conditions.*
 
 
 
• **'At' **will be used with disgust when there is something temporary but if there is a habit or regular thing, we will prefer using **'with'**. *​​***​**__

__**Correct sentence:**__ *Ankita is disgusted **with** the habit of her brother. *
